events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The rider was quoted $12.71 at 1× surge, and the fare rose to $16.17 at 1.4× from trip start, so the difference of $3.46 is entirely a surge change [F6][F7][F8]. That brings the case under SURGE-2 and SURGE-3, and the notice in the platform's surge log is the operative question [F9][SURGE-1].

I read the notice text as a careful person would. It names the new multiplier ("Fares are 1.4× higher right now"), it states a revised estimated fare ("Your new estimated fare is $17.29"), and it states a free cancellation ("You can cancel for free") [F9]. All three items SURGE-1 requires are present, and none is vague or self-contradicting; no "fees may apply" style hedge appears [F9][SURGE-1]. The quoted estimate of $17.29 differing from the $16.17 finally charged does not undo the notice — an estimate that differs from the final fare is still a stated estimate [F7][F9]. The notice was logged at 17:18:45, before the trip started at 17:20:00, so it satisfied the before-or-at-pickup timing [F9][SURGE-1]. The rider's own captured messages are only pickup arrangements and contain no denial of notice [F10][F11][F12]; in any event the platform log outweighs a bare statement that no notice arrived [F9][SURGE-1].

With notice complete and the rider having ridden, the higher fare stands: SURGE-2 gives no_action for surge risen with the rider notified [F9][SURGE-1][SURGE-2]. The trace's formula is therefore not applied: the allowed surge figure is (1.4 − 1) × surgeable subtotal $10.66 = $4.26, capped at the $3.46 the fare exceeds the quote, but it is refundable only when notice is missing, which it is not [F8][SURGE-3]. Amount: $0.00.

The rider's profile flag for repeated fare disputes does not decide anything here; the profile never settles the current case, and the driver's record shows no upheld route deviation [F14][F15][RD-6]. On the safety screen I read every chat message, the driver's written statement and the complaint: they concern price and route, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is clear [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1]. The records needed for this ruling are all present — GPS distances, the fare breakdown, the timestamped notice and timestamped chat — so no evidence gap exists [F1][F3][F5][F9][F12][TH-4].
